svg.title: The macro census used here has a period qualification, already included in the step hypotheses. Put R = j +8. The macro box radius is (j +7)L. If twice this radius is smaller than the fine period, two displacements in that box with the same periodic image coincide, coordinate by coordinate. Thus M(i, z) ≤1. A nonzero multiplicity also implies dist(i, parent z) ≤R: multiply the coarse distance by L, use the distance from the embedded base to z, at most (j + 7)L, and the fine site’s distance to its embedded parent, at most L/2. The triangle inequality gives the stated integer bound. Consequently X
